ID: COLBOG2 							
Country: Colombia							
City: Bogotá							
Period: January- June 1808							
Resolution: Daily							
Observers: Francisco José de Caldas 							
Location Observatory: 4.59, -74.07 (2650masl)							
Meteorological variables:  Maximum and minimum barometer (Column 4, 5) (lines of the king's foot); indoor and outdoor temperature (Column 6, 7) (Reamur), precipitation (Column 8) (king's foot)							
Data source: Observaciones meteorologicas hechas en el Observatorio astronomico de Santa Fe de Bogata por D. Francisco José de Caldas. Semanario de la Nueva Granada 1849.							
Descriptive Name: BOGOTA_1808							
Other comments: The documentary source provides the conversion factor 1 king's foot is 1.935 mm. This seems to be an error because this conversion factor corresponds from Castilian lines to millimeters, being more plausible that the precipitation was recorded in Castilian lines. The indoor and outdoor temperatures are recorded in Reaumur, the first have been record with a Dollond thermometer in the main hall of the observatory, the other thermometer were built by the same artist and is identical to the first, this thermometer is outdoors, 10 varas above the garden ground. Three measurements were record and the arithmetic mean is in column 6 and 7.							
Barometer: The mercurial purification, the scale and the fill procedure have been done with all the care possible. The mercury have been boiled out an in the tube.
